title: Multimode phonon-mediated enhancement of entanglement and competing synchronization in cavity magnomechanics
authors: Z. Imara, Jia-Xin Peng, E. K. Berinyuy, S. K. Singh, A. El Allati
abstract: The generation of quantum correlations in hybrid quantum systems remains a central challenge due to the intrinsic limitations of linear interactions. In cavity magnomechanical platforms, the cavity-magnon coupling gives rise to hybridized cavity-magnon polaritons (CMPs). However, as a beam-splitter-type interaction, it does not by itself generate entanglement between the polariton modes in the absence of additional nonlinear or parametric processes. Here, we propose a mechanism based on multimode phonon mediation, in which multiple vibrational modes act as parallel scattering channels that couple the polaritons through Stokes and anti-Stokes processes. We show that , in the parameter regime explored here, the presence of multiple phonon modes leads to a monotonic enhancement of steady-state entanglement, thereby going beyond the limitations of conventional single-mode schemes. Furthermore, we demonstrate that quantum synchronization between the polariton modes originates from the same underlying scattering processes responsible for entanglement generation, yet exhibits an opposite scaling behavior with increasing phonon number for the phase quadrature, while the amplitude synchronization reveals collective squeezing that grows with the number of phonon channels. Our results provide new insights into the role of multimode interactions in shaping quantum correlations and establish a viable pathway for controlling entanglement and collective dynamics in hybrid magnomechanical platforms.
summary: The paper proposes that utilizing multiple vibrational phonon modes as parallel scattering channels can overcome the inherent limitations of linear coupling in cavity magnomechanics to generate robust quantum entanglement. This multimode mediation enhances entanglement monotonically while simultaneously inducing collective amplitude squeezing, offering a pathway for controlling quantum resources in these hybrid systems.
main_problem: The central challenge is generating quantum entanglement between cavity-magnon polariton modes, which are inherently limited by linear beam-splitter interactions.
main_result: Multimode phonon mediation provides a mechanism that monotonically enhances steady-state bipartite entanglement and generates collective squeezing in the amplitude quadrature of the polaritons.
method: The analysis uses Quantum Langevin Equations (QLEs) linearized around the steady state to calculate quantum fluctuations, followed by solving Lyapunov equations for covariance matrix evolution.
model_or_system: The system is a cavity magnomechanical platform involving coupled microwave cavity ($	ext{a}$), magnon ($	ext{c}$), and multiple vibrational/phonon modes ($k$ modes). The coupling forms hybridized polaritons ($	ext{p}^\pm$).
key_observables: Logarithmic negativity (bipartite entanglement, EN); minimum residual conrangle (tripartite entanglement, Rmin^tau); quantum synchronization measures ($S_c, S_x, S_\phi$)
important_parameters: Number of phonon modes ($k$); detunings ($\Delta_\pm$); coupling strengths ($G_{0j}$); operating temperature and damping rates.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a dispersive interaction regime and linearizes the QLEs, neglecting higher-order fluctuation terms.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate entanglement dependence on phonon frequency spacing and mode number; they also show robustness against temperature and damping rates, and quantify synchronization measures vs. $k$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical model and the limitation of single-mode coupling. It then develops the theoretical framework using QLEs to analyze quantum fluctuations. The core results demonstrate how multimode phonon scattering enhances entanglement while simultaneously affecting different synchronization quadratures.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses open quantum systems dynamics in a complex hybrid platform, providing quantitative measures for controlling non-classical correlations (entanglement and squeezing) using engineered environmental coupling channels (phonons).

figures.caption: FIG. 1: (a) Schematic of the multimode polaromechani- cal system. Strong coupling between the microwave cavity mode a and magnon mode c creates two hybrid cavity– magnon polariton (CMP) modes p+ and p−. Each po- lariton dispersively couples to k mechanical modes (bj, j = 1, . . . , k) via magnetostriction. (b) Frequency dia- gram. The magnon mode is driven at frequency ω0, and phonons scatter the driving photons onto Stokes (ω0 −ω1) and anti-Stokes (ω0 + ω1) sidebands. Setting the polariton frequencies resonant with the sidebands, ω−≃ω0 −ω1 and ω+ ≃ω0 + ω1, enables entanglement between the two polaritons via collective phonon mediation.

FIG. 2: Effect of the phonon frequency spacing ∆ω on the polariton-polariton entanglement and on the tripartite entan- glement. (a)-(c) Spectral configurations for k = 2, k = 6, and k = 12 phonon modes, respectively. Three spacings are considered in each panel: ∆ω/2π = 2 MHz (I), ∆ω/2π = 5 MHz (II), and ∆ω/2π = 10 MHz (III). The first phonon mode is fixed at ω1/2π = 10 MHz (dashed red line). Green bars indicate the optimal configuration maximizing EN. The corre- sponding value of EN is indicated below each configuration. (d) Bipartite entanglement E p+p− N and (e) genuine tripartite entanglement Rmin τ (p+, p−, b1) as continuous functions of the phonon frequency spacing ∆ω for k = 2, 6, 12,...

Markers indicate the maxi- mum EN for each k. (b) Maximum entanglement Emax N as a function of the number of phonon modes k. The parame- ters are the same as in Fig. 2.

Fig. 4(a) shows the stationary polariton entanglement EN as a function of the mixing angle θ for k = 2, 6, 12, 25, and 50 phonon modes. The system is dynami- cally unstable for θ/π ≲0.25, a regime where the Stokes and anti-Stokes scattering rates are nearly balanced and no stationary entanglement can be sustained. Beyond this threshold, EN exhibits a pronounced peak whose amplitude grows monotonically with k: Emax N ≃0.14 (k = 2), 0.20 (k = 6), 0.24 (k = 12), 0.28 (k = 25), and 0.33 (k = 50), representing more than a twofold en- hancement relative to the k = 2 case. Spintronics.note: The new paper analyzes a cavity magnomechanical platform involving magnon polaritons and coupling to cavities, which directly falls under the scope of quantum-optics concepts applied to magnetic systems (magnons/spin waves coupled to cavity photons).
